data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 0. The obstruction structures are locally stable mixed configurations where each color class is a disjoint union of cycles and the crossing edges form a perfect matching between opposite-color cycles. The expected number of such frozen cycle configurations scales like \u0398(n) per vertex, so the fraction of configurations that are stable mixed is bounded away from 0, and consensus is not reached whp.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the dynamics cannot reach these cycle-based configurations from a uniform random start because they require a large number of coordinated flips, the probability of consensus may be higher.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the number of 2-factors is o(n) rather than exponential, the scaling law fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"On a random 3-regular graph, one can construct many stable mixed configurations by taking a 2-factor of the graph and coloring its cycles alternately. These configurations are absorbing because every vertex has two same-color neighbors and one opposite-color neighbor. Since random 3-regular graphs have many 2-factors, the process has a positive probability of being trapped in one of these cycle-based obstructions.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
